scope.summary: The harness reaches Expat parsing, parser creation, external parser inheritance, and buffer handling. It does not exercise the new reparse deferral mechanism: each parser receives one nonfinal parse call followed immediately by a final parse call. The supplied scope therefore is not sufficient.

blockers.requirement: Exercise the default-enabled reparse deferral mechanism for a partial XML token through successive nonfinal parse calls on the same parser.
blockers.target_route: A finite XML document with a long token can be split across nonfinal XML_Parse calls; after the first incomplete-token attempt, a later small nonfinal increment with buffer capacity available can make have_now less than twice had_before and defer processing.
blockers.failure_condition: ParseOneInput passes all bytes once with isFinal=0 and then all bytes again with isFinal=1. The first call starts with had_before=0, so it cannot defer; the second call bypasses the deferral guard because finalBuffer is true. The entry repeats this pattern on freshly created parsers.
blockers.alternative_paths: The namespace and external parsers use the same helper sequence. External parser creation copies the enabled setting but initializes a fresh partial-token count. Zero-length input, reset, and the final call provide no equivalent later nonfinal attempt.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: Initialization sets the prior partial-token count to zero and enables deferral by default.
